name: Counter 3-4-1-2

slots.why: Wide centre-back who defends the channel. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the ball-playing defender in the middle starts the counters, so the outside pair only has to defend. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Ball-playing defender in the centre starts counters with a forward pass.

Cover centre-back sweeps up behind his partner and the wing-back's space. Defend is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the ball-playing defender in the middle starts the counters, so the outside pair only has to defend. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Support wing-back gives width but holds a safer position on this side.
Attacking wing-back is the team's main wide threat when the ball is won.
Defensive central midfielder screens the back three and lets his partner go forward.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the counter with runs from deep.
Attacking midfielder is the link between the midfield and two strikers, receiving between the lines.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds up the ball so others can join the counter.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A cautious back-three system retaining an AMC and two strikers so regains can become attacks without waiting for many players to advance.
whyGood: The AMC, DLF and AF form an immediate counter-attacking triangle while the back three protect against turnovers.
whyThisShape: A back three, wing-backs, two central midfielders and an attacking midfielder behind two strikers. It defends with five or six players, then breaks quickly through the two forwards and the attacking midfielder.
whenToUse: Against stronger sides that will have most of the ball, or when your squad has quick forwards and dependable centre-backs.
whenNotToUse: When you need to dominate the game, or when your wing-backs cannot defend as well as they run.

instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Let the opposition advance before engaging, keeping space for the forward outlets after a regain.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
